chunks: Hishām ibn Sālim asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman: may she lead women? He said:
She may lead them in the supererogatory prayer; but as for the obligatory prayer, no. And she should not stand in front of them; rather, she stands in their midst.

key_terms.النِّسَاءَ: the women being led in congregation
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman being asked about in the ruling
key_terms.تَؤُمُّ: to lead others in salat (prayer) as Imam
key_terms.تَتَقَدَّمُهُنَّ: to stand in front of them

ai.seo_question: Can a woman lead other women in prayer according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on a woman leading other women in salat (prayer). It states that she may lead them in supererogatory prayers, but not in obligatory prayers, and if she leads, she stands among them rather than ahead of them.
